requirements.necessity: The exponential function e^x is defined for all real x, so it imposes no restriction on the domain.

requirements.name: continuity_of_sum
requirements.necessity: The sum of two continuous functions is continuous on the intersection of their domains. Thus, once the domain is determined, continuity follows automatically.

requirements.name: continuity_of_product
requirements.necessity: The product of two continuous functions is continuous. The term x·e^x is a product of continuous functions on ℝ, so it is continuous everywhere.

passages.content: Many functions have the property that their graphs can be traced with a pencil without lifting the pencil from the page. Such functions are called continuous. Other functions have points at which a break in the graph occurs, but satisfy this property over intervals contained in their domains.
